panel.says: one row per entity per period: every ("ISO3", "Year") pair in this table is unique, so rowCount (2910) counts readings, never subjects — there are 194 of those
panel.decidedBy: every ("ISO3", "Year") pair is unique across all 2910 rows, and "ISO3" holds no blank

coverage.says: a period's own step being present is not the same as every entity being present in it: the fullest period here carries 194 entities and the thinnest carries 194

aggregates.says: an aggregate here is a row of this table that is the SUM of other rows of the same table. byArithmetic is DECIDED from the numbers: the same set of rows adds up to it in every period. byStructure is a proposal and nothing more — a row whose code is shaped unlike the rest of the column, or missing from it — and it also sweeps in places whose code is merely unusual. Take a proposal as a question to put to the journalist, never as an answer.

arithmetic.reason: the structural test set no row of this table apart, so there was no candidate to put to the arithmetic — a set of rows that happens to add up to another is a coincidence until something else says that row is different

structure.reason: no column of this table holds one stable code per entity with a shape most of them share

claims.sentence: A total of 38 deaths have been reported, based on preliminary data received as of 6 March 2025.
Reporting for the most recent months is therefore incomplete and provisional, and the table's 2025 rows are the publisher's placeholder zeros, not observations.

statedIncompleteness.says: the frozen prose states that a period this table holds is incomplete — a CLAIM the journalist wrote, carried here with the sentence that made it, never a fact this profiler checked
